explanations: terra: A غِشَاوَةٌ lies over the deniers' sight and a great punishment awaits them, a different use of the section's covering root that makes prior blindness lead toward punishment.

luna: This verse says the person whose evil and sin encompass him belongs to the Fire; it makes the section's unpleasant end of sin a settled destination. | terra: Whoever earns an evil and is encompassed by his offense becomes a companion of the Fire; the offense itself closes around its doer and carries him to its end.
luna: When told to fear God, the arrogant person is carried into sin and ends in Hell; this shows the opposite response to the caution the section says warning is meant to produce.
terra: What is in heaven and earth belongs to God; hidden and open contents are brought to account, after which He forgives or punishes, making ownership the frame of judgment.

luna: The section's sin-to-punishment link also appears in this account of Pharaoh's people, who denied signs and were seized for their sins. | terra: God seizes Pharaoh's people and their predecessors بِذُنُوبِهِمْ, then calls Him شَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ; the ayah itself joins the section's sin and following-punishment roots.
luna: The section glosses ر ب ب as owner and says the camel belongs to Allah; this verse calls God مالك الملك, the owner of sovereignty who gives and takes dominion.
terra: Heaven and earth belong to God, who forgives or punishes whom He wills; this repeated owner-to-judgment formula supports the section's reading of Rabb as proprietor.

luna: The section names ع ق ب for what follows an act; this verse invites the reader to see the end of earlier deniers, the same outcome pattern as Thamud. | terra: The audience is told to travel and inspect the عَاقِبَة of the deniers, treating an act of rejection as something understood through its historical end.
luna: The verse redirects fear away from human enemies and toward God, a specific human counterpart to the section's claim that God's warning is meant to make people cautious.
luna: Disbelievers are not to mistake their respite for good: it lets them increase in sin before humiliating punishment, a specific delayed-consequence pattern.
terra: The punishment is identified as what their hands sent ahead, and God denies injustice to His servants; the result is the offender's own act arriving before him.
luna: The section praises one who purifies the soul; this verse draws a boundary against self-congratulation, saying God purifies whom He wills and people must not claim purity for themselves.
luna: The verse says whoever earns sin earns it against himself, an explicit individual-accountability formulation of the section's punishment for one's own sin.
terra: Whoever does evil is recompensed for it and finds no protector or helper against God, joining deed, due result, and inability to avert it.
terra: God's ownership of the heavens and earth is stated immediately before His freedom to punish or forgive, directly supporting the section's movement from owner to recompense.
terra: If the addressees turn away from God's judgment, He intends to strike them for some of their ذُنُوبِهِمْ; the offense is again named as the cause of the blow that follows.
terra: فَأَهْلَكْنَاهُم بِذُنُوبِهِمْ exactly repeats destruction because of sins and then describes another generation raised after them, sharpening the sequence of deed, end, and successor.

luna: The repeated command to travel and see the end of those who denied gives another concrete use of the section's end-of-deniers pattern. | terra: Travel through the earth and inspect the عَاقِبَة of the deniers repeats the section's method of reading guilt by the terminal evidence it leaves.
luna: If God sends harm, no one can remove it but Him; this gives another concrete formulation of the section's claim that no one can reverse His consequence.
luna: Like the section's denied warning followed by punishment, this verse says punishment touches those who deny God's signs because they persist in defiance.
luna: The verse says judgment belongs only to God and that He relates the truth, directly complementing the section's account of a Lord whose judgment has no mu'aqqib.
terra: People are returned to God, their true master; judgment belongs to Him and He is swift in account, joining ownership, return, and the final ruling after which nothing remains.

luna: The source image has night covering its object; here night comes over Abraham before he watches a star set. The scene parallels night as a covering, though its context is a different argument about celestial signs.
terra: The Lord's word is completed in truth and justice and no one can alter His words, giving the promised outcome its truth and irreversibility.
luna: The section defines ذ ن ب through the unpleasant end of an act; this verse says those who earn sin will be repaid for what they used to commit.

luna: No soul earns except against itself and no bearer carries another's burden; this clarifies the section's emphasis that Thamud were taken for their own sin. | terra: Each soul earns only against itself, no bearer carries another's burden, and all return to their Lord; this fixes each consequence to its own offender and final Owner.
luna: The scales on the Day are declared true and those whose scales are heavy succeed, a judgment scene that parallels the section's success-and-failure outcomes.
luna: Those whose scales are light lose themselves for wronging the signs, the other outcome of the weighing begun in 7:8.
luna: Every community has an appointed term that cannot be advanced or delayed when it arrives, clarifying the time-bound end announced to Thamud.

luna: The verse pictures Fire as coverings above its people, a punitive enclosure that parallels the section's enveloping punishment. | terra: Hell is both bedding below and coverings above, followed by وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلظَّالِمِينَ; enclosure is expressly the wrongdoers' recompense.

luna: Salih calls the she-camel Allah's sign and warns against harming her; the section's account of the Lord punishing those who attack what is His grows from this scene. | terra: The camel is نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ and a sign, allowed to eat on God's earth, while harm to her is tied immediately to painful punishment; the owner's creature and the owner's response stand together.

luna: The people hamstring the she-camel after rejecting the warning, the concrete wrong that the section identifies as preceding Thamud's end. | terra: Thamud hamstring the camel, defy their Lord's command, and demand the threatened result; this gives the precise crime whose consequence the image places at its heel.

luna: The earthquake seizes them and leaves them fallen in their homes, giving the punishment following the camel's slaughter a physical end. | terra: The earthquake takes them and leaves them fallen in their home, supplying the concrete outcome of the camel-killing and challenge in 7:77.
terra: After Thamud's destruction, Salih says he delivered his Lord's message and advised them but they did not love advisers; this completes the camel episode's warning stance.

luna: After Lot's people are destroyed, the verse tells the reader to see the end of criminals, another punishment followed by its stated outcome. | terra: After the punitive rain on Lot's people, the reader is told to inspect the عَاقِبَة of the criminals, explicitly joining crime-language to the end of the scene.
terra: Shuayb's people are told to inspect the عَاقِبَة of corrupters after being warned against blocking and distorting God's way, making the social offense legible in its end.

luna: The section follows denial with punishment; this verse supplies the reverse boundary, saying belief and God-consciousness would have opened blessings, while denial brought seizure for what people earned.
terra: The townspeople feel secure from punishment coming by night while they sleep, exposing false human fearlessness before an unexpected consequence.
terra: The townspeople likewise feel secure from punishment arriving by day during play, completing the warning that no ordinary setting makes the threatened end avoidable.

luna: In a passage about towns that rejected messengers, this verse asks whether people feel secure from God's plan; only the losers feel secure, the human boundary to 91:15's divine non-fear. | terra: Those who feel secure from God's plan are called losers; their false absence of fear is the human opposite of the Lord's rightful lack of fear about His decree.
terra: After Pharaoh's people wrongfully reject the signs, the reader is told to inspect the عَاقِبَة of corrupters, another sign-denial ending in judgment.

luna: Moses says the good end belongs to the God-fearing, a positive boundary to the destructive end of Thamud and the section's sin-consequence link. | terra: Moses tells his people that the earth belongs to God and that ٱلْعَاقِبَةُ belongs to the Godfearing; ownership and the good end meet, though outside the purification wording itself.
luna: The root غ ش و named for the section's night and covering punishment also describes protective slumber here; the contrast shows that being covered can secure rather than punish.
luna: The preceding verse describes angels striking the faces and backs of disbelievers as they die; 8:51 gives the reason as what their hands sent ahead.

luna: This neighboring statement makes the moral basis of 8:54 explicit: what befell them was for what their hands had sent ahead, and God wrongs no servants. | terra: The same formula says the punishment is what their hands sent ahead and that God does not wrong His servants, defining the consequence as earned rather than arbitrary.

luna: This sets up 8:54's Pharaoh parallel by saying those earlier people disbelieved God's signs and were seized for their sins. | terra: The Pharaoh pattern is repeated as God seizing them بِذُنُوبِهِمْ and being severe in ٱلْعِقَابِ, an explicit lexical meeting of offense and its sequel.
luna: Between the Pharaoh parallels in 8:52 and 8:54, this verse says God does not change a favor until people change what is in themselves, spelling out human agency before punishment.

luna: The source section itself cites this parallel: Pharaoh's people denied the signs and were destroyed for their sins, making the link between ذنب and punishment explicit. | terra: The deniers are destroyed بِذُنُوبِهِمْ and Pharaoh's people drowned; this is the same causal wording as 91:14 and makes the punishment the second thing following denial.
terra: Thamud are among peoples whose messengers brought proofs; God did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves, placing responsibility for their end on their own act.

terra: Unlike the night-covered faces of evildoers in 10:27, the good-doers' faces are covered by neither darkness nor humiliation; this is the section's digestible good end pictured as the absence of a punitive cover.

luna: The verse joins evil deeds and their recompense to humiliation covering faces like a piece of dark night, closely meeting the section's night-as-enveloping-punishment image. | terra: Bad deeds receive an equal recompense, humiliation overtakes their doers, and their faces are as though covered with dark pieces of night; this ayah fuses consequence, غ ش و covering, and the section's night image.
luna: Each soul is confronted with what it sent ahead and returned to its true Lord, joining the section's end-of-deed image with return to the owner.

luna: This verse tells the reader to look at the end of wrongdoers who denied what they did not understand, linking denial to its result. | terra: They deny what they have not comprehended before its fulfillment reaches them, then the reader is told to inspect the عَاقِبَة of the wrongdoers; premature denial carries a later disclosed end.

luna: No one can remove harm or repel the good God wills, another direct statement of the finality behind the section's no-reverser image. | terra: If God touches someone with harm none can remove it, and if He intends good none can repel His bounty; the ayah states the no-reversal principle on both sides of outcome.
luna: This verse describes punishment postponed to a named term and then impossible to turn away, paralleling Salih's three-day deadline and certain promise.
terra: No protector can save from God's command on the flood day except one receiving mercy, a concrete disaster-scene boundary on any attempt to avert divine judgment.

luna: After Noah's account, the verse says the good end is for the God-fearing, contrasting the lasting outcome of heedfulness with punishment. | terra: The Prophet is told to be patient because ٱلْعَاقِبَةَ is for the Godfearing, a direct positive counterpart to Thamud's disastrous outcome.
luna: Salih tells Thamud that God brought them from the earth and settled them there, then calls them to seek forgiveness; this adds the creator-and-owner basis before the camel warning.
luna: Thamud reject Salih's call and say they doubt what he invites them to, giving a fuller instance of the denial that precedes their camel offense.
luna: Salih asks who could protect him from God if he disobeyed Him; this makes the section's claim that no one can overturn the Lord's consequence concrete within the Thamud story.

luna: This is Salih's warning about Allah's she-camel as a sign: leave her alone or a painful punishment will seize them, the same warning-and-consequence relation as in the section. | terra: Salih calls her نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ and God's sign, then warns that touching her with harm will bring a near punishment; ownership, trespass, warning, and consequence are all explicit.

luna: After they hamstring the she-camel, Salih gives the people three days in their homes and calls the promise unfalse; the short delay makes the stated end measurable. | terra: After they hamstring the camel, Salih gives them three days and calls the deadline a promise that will not be falsified, exactly staging the delayed but uncancellable end described in the section.

luna: After the three-day warning, God saves Salih and the believers by mercy; their rescue marks a boundary between the offenders' end and those who heed. | terra: When the command arrives, Salih and the believers are saved by mercy while the camel-killers proceed to disgrace, showing the Lord's judgment distinguishing innocent from guilty.

luna: The blast seizes the wrongdoers and leaves them fallen in their homes, completing the three-day warning in 11:65. | terra: The blast seizes the wrongdoers and leaves them fallen in their dwellings, contributing the actual punishment that fulfills the three-day word of 11:65.

luna: The verse says Thamud seemed never to have lived there and names their rejection of their Lord, describing how complete their end was. | terra: Thamud's end is pictured as if they had never flourished in their homes; the ayah completes 11:65 by making the promised sequel erase the offenders' settled life.
luna: After the prophet stories, God says He did not wrong the towns but they wronged themselves and their false gods did not avail them, clarifying the justice behind punishment for sin.
luna: This verse names God's painful, severe seizure of wrongdoing towns, distilling the consequence that the Thamud narrative has just shown.
luna: The preceding seizure is called a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter, directly matching the section's warning-as-caution claim.

luna: The section quotes غاشية من عذاب الله for punishment that envelops; this verse asks whether people feel safe from a غاشية of God's punishment arriving suddenly. | terra: The ayah asks whether they feel safe from a غَاشِيَةٌ مِّنْ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ or a sudden Hour, exactly supplying the section's dictionary image of an all-covering divine punishment.
terra: The reader is told to inspect the عَاقِبَة of former peoples and then that the final home is better for the Godfearing, placing bad historical ends beside the favorable enduring one.

luna: The source section names the root ع ق ب through مُعَقِّب, one who follows another's heels; this verse uses its related form for watchers before and behind a person, then says God changes a people's state when they change themselves. | terra: مُعَقِّبَاتٌ are placed before and behind a person, and the ayah ends by saying that when God wills harm there is no repeller or protector; it joins the bodily behind/heel image to an irreversible consequence.

luna: Those who patiently meet hardship and answer evil with good receive the good end of the Home, a positive use of the section's end/recompense theme. | terra: Patient worshippers who answer evil with good are promised عُقْبَى ٱلدَّارِ, making the end attached to purified conduct the reverse of Thamud's end.
terra: The angels greet the patient with peace and call their destination نِعْمَ عُقْبَى ٱلدَّارِ, naming the good sequel of the conduct listed in 13:22.
terra: Messengers are mocked, the disbelievers receive respite, and then God seizes them; the ayah asks how His punishment was, precisely staging delay followed by consequence.
luna: The section sets the end of sin against purification's success; this verse calls the garden the end of the God-fearing and the Fire the end of disbelievers.

luna: The section names the root ع ق ب in عُقْبَٰهَا as an end and a recompense, then cites this formulation: no معقب can overturn God's judgment. | terra: The source section's dictionary form مُعَقِّب is spoken here as لَا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ: God's judgment has no follower who can reverse it, directly unfolding the finality of 91:15.
terra: After 13:41 denies any reverser of God's judgment, this ayah says all planning belongs to God and disbelievers will learn who has عُقْبَى ٱلدَّارِ; it adds the final outcome of rival plots.
luna: God is not unaware of wrongdoers but postpones them to a day when eyes stare, a direct parallel to announced respite followed by an inescapable end.
terra: God never fails His promise to His messengers and is mighty in retribution, directly supporting the unfalsifiable promise that followed Thamud's crime.
terra: The criminals wear pitch and fire تَغْشَىٰ وُجُوهَهُم; with 14:51 this makes covering the bodily form taken by recompense.
terra: God repays every soul what it earned immediately after fire is said to cover the criminals' faces in 14:50, identifying the cover as the act's due sequel.
terra: The evils of what they did strike them and what they mocked surrounds them, turning the deed into the enclosing consequence that follows it.
terra: Every nation receives a messenger commanding worship and avoidance of false gods, and the reader is told to inspect the عَاقِبَة of the deniers; warning precedes the visible end.
terra: Those who plot evil are asked whether they feel secure from being swallowed by the earth or struck unexpectedly, tying criminal plotting to the danger they fail to fear.
terra: God may seize the plotters amid their movements and they cannot frustrate Him, making the warned consequence impossible to outrun.
terra: God may seize the plotters through gradual diminution, a secondary use of the fear root's form that adds slow reduction to the sudden punishments of 16:45-46.

luna: God does not seize people for every wrong at once but delays them to an appointed term; this makes the three-day reprieve intelligible as a fixed limit. | terra: If God seized people for wrongdoing no creature would remain, yet He delays them to a term that can be neither postponed nor advanced once it comes.
terra: What people possess comes to an end while what is with God remains, and the patient are repaid by their best deeds; it makes permanence the measure of the favorable sequel.

terra: Human retaliation, عَاقِبُوا, is limited to the like of what was suffered and patience is called better; the penalty-after-offense root is retained while human recompense is placed under a strict boundary.
terra: Good is done for oneself and evil against oneself, then the final promise arrives; the ayah explicitly lets the chosen act carry its later promised end.
terra: Each person's enduring fate is fastened to his neck and will be brought out as a record, a bodily attachment that makes the later consequence inseparable from the doer.
luna: The verse says no one bears another's burden and that God does not punish until sending a messenger, linking personal consequence to the warning Salih delivered.

luna: This is the very sign of Thamud, the she-camel, and the verse says signs are sent as تخويفا, warning that urges caution, as the section explains. | terra: The ayah names Thamud's she-camel as a visible sign they wronged and says signs are sent only as تَخْوِيفًا; it supplies the exact warning function the section assigns the camel.
terra: No one can change the Lord's words and no refuge exists besides Him, supporting the section's claim that the final divine word admits neither revision nor escape.
luna: This verse says the Fire's walls will surround the wrongdoers, a concrete image of punishment enclosing those who reject warning.
terra: The proud gardener's fruit is encompassed by ruin and he turns his hands over what he spent; the act's hidden end becomes visible before 18:44 names the true owner and best outcome.
terra: He has no company to help him against God and cannot defend himself, contributing the no-reversal element between the ruin of 18:42 and God's final authority in 18:44.

luna: After the garden owner's wealth fails and no group helps, the verse says God's protection is true and names the better reward and end with عُقْبًا. | terra: At the ruined garden, authority belongs to God alone and He is best in reward and عُقْبًا; ownership and the ultimately good outcome meet in the very aftermath of loss.
terra: The record makes the guilty fearful, omits neither small nor great, and leaves them finding what they did present; their feared future is their own deed made inescapably present.

luna: God would hasten punishment for what people earned but gives them an appointed term; this tightly joins the section's sin-consequence theme to Thamud's three-day respite. | terra: The merciful Lord could seize people immediately for what they earned but gives them an appointed time from which they find no escape, closely paralleling Thamud's fixed delay.
luna: The criminal who comes to his Lord has Hell and neither dies nor lives there, a direct negative counterpart to the reward of the purified in 20:76.
luna: The next verse gives high ranks to the believer who has done righteous deeds, completing the positive side of the criminal-versus-purified contrast.
luna: The verse names the lasting gardens as reward for whoever comes purified, connecting the section's success through purification with its eventual recompense.
terra: A believer who does right fears neither injustice nor diminution, showing the human freedom from fear granted by a sound deed's end rather than the sovereign fearlessness of the Judge.
terra: After the command to persist in prayer, وَٱلْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ states that the enduring end belongs to reverence, matching the section's favorable sequel of purified conduct.

luna: The section says the Lord who brings the consequence is not afraid of its aftermath; this verse states that He is not questioned for what He does, while they are questioned. | terra: God is not questioned about what He does while they are questioned, directly stating the asymmetry by which the Lord need not fear the aftermath of His judgment.
luna: God sets just scales so no soul is wronged, even by a mustard seed's weight; this states the fairness behind the section's judgment for each person's sin.
terra: Those established in the land uphold worship and right conduct, and to God belongs عَاقِبَةُ ٱلْأُمُورِ; responsible action is placed before the Owner's final outcome.
terra: Thamud are named among the peoples who denied messengers before the present deniers, supplying a specific precedent for the respite-and-seizure pattern completed in 22:44.
terra: Moses is denied, the deniers receive respite, and then God seizes them; the sequence reinforces that postponement never falsifies the threatened end.
luna: Many a wrongdoing town is given respite before being seized; the verse then says all return to God, parallel to the section's delay followed by outcome.
terra: One who retaliates only in the measure suffered and is then attacked is promised God's help; the ayah bounds human punishment even while using the section's following-recompense root.
terra: Sovereignty over everything is in God's hand; He protects while none can protect against Him, directly uniting ownership with unanswerable judgment.
luna: The verse calls night a garment and sleep repose, a specific restful use of the night-covering scene that contrasts with the section's night as punitive covering.

terra: Moses says the Egyptians hold a ذَنبٌ against him and therefore he fears they will kill him; a human agent expects a harmful sequel to an offense, precisely reversing God's lack of fear after judgment.
luna: Thamud dismiss Salih as bewitched, a particular form of the denial that the section says began their crime.
luna: They challenge Salih to produce a sign because he is human; the next ayah gives the camel, completing the scene behind the section's account.

luna: The camel and the people have their appointed turns to drink, a specific detail of the camel provision they violate when they hamstring her. | terra: Salih identifies the camel and her allotted drink alongside the people's allotted day; with 26:156 it specifies the protected property and measured right they violate.

luna: Salih warns them not to touch the she-camel with harm lest a great day's punishment seize them, directly joining the sign, transgression, and consequence. | terra: The command not to touch the camel with harm is coupled to seizure by the punishment of a tremendous day, directly binding trespass to its warned end.

luna: The people hamstring her and become regretful; this is the act whose aftermath the section traces. | terra: They hamstring her and then become regretful, making remorse the first consequence immediately behind the crime before the punishment of 26:158.

luna: The punishment then seizes them; the verse makes the consequence of the camel's slaughter explicit. | terra: The punishment takes the camel-killers after their regret in 26:157, completing the section's sequence from offense to inescapable recompense.
terra: The completed camel-and-punishment story is declared a sign, and God is named the mighty, merciful Lord; this interprets the event itself as warning under its owner.
terra: The punishment of the day of the overshadowing cloud seizes Shuayb's deniers, an indirect collective parallel to punishment arriving in a covering form.
terra: The deniers ask to hasten God's punishment, a stance matching Thamud's demand that the warned sequel be brought.
terra: The ayah asks the reader to consider even years of temporary enjoyment, setting up the limited interval before the promise in 26:206.
terra: After the imagined long respite, the promised result comes to them; the lapse between crime and consequence changes neither its truth nor arrival.
terra: Their former enjoyment does not benefit them once the promise comes, showing that what preceded the final judgment cannot stand after it.

luna: The verse says the arrogant rejected signs despite inward certainty and asks the reader to see the end of corrupters, a direct denial-and-outcome pattern. | terra: They reject the signs unjustly despite inward certainty, and the reader is told to see the عَاقِبَة of the corrupters; culpable denial is interpreted by its ending.

luna: This identifies the nine plotters in the section's cited Neml account as corrupters who would not reform, before their plot and its outcome. | terra: Nine men are identified in the city as corrupters who do not set things right; this supplies the criminal band whose plot reaches its عَاقِبَة in 27:51.

luna: This is the nine-person plot whose عاقبة the section cites in 27:51: they swear to kill Salih and his family by night and conceal it from his kin. | terra: The nine swear to kill Salih and his family at night and then lie to his heir, specifying the guilty act whose terminal result 27:51 tells the reader to inspect.

luna: The next verse says they plotted while God planned against them without their awareness, completing the plot whose outcome 27:51 names. | terra: They devise a plot and God devises one while they do not perceive it, showing the hidden counter-sequence already following their crime before 27:51 announces its end.

luna: This is the section's cited example: look at the عاقبة of the nine plotters' scheme, which ends in the destruction of them and their people. | terra: The ayah explicitly makes the عَاقِبَة of the nine men's plot their own destruction together with their people, the exact Thamud instance of an act carrying its end behind it.

luna: The plot's aftermath is shown as empty houses because of their wrongdoing, giving 27:51's destruction a visible trace. | terra: Their houses stand empty because they wronged, leaving a visible remainder of the destruction stated in 27:51 and making the crime legible through its aftermath.

luna: Beside the destroyed plotters, this verse says God saved those who believed and were God-conscious, the contrasting outcome of heeding the warning. | terra: God saves those who believed and were mindful immediately after the plotters' ruined houses in 27:52, providing the opposite outcome under the same Owner.
terra: After the killing, Moses leaves the city fearful and watchful, embodying a human actor's expectation that an adverse result may follow his earlier deed.
terra: Moses says he killed one of them and fears they will kill him, restaging fear as expectation that an adverse consequence will follow one's prior act.
terra: Pharaoh and his hosts are seized and cast into the sea, then the reader is told to see the عَاقِبَة of wrongdoers; the bodily punishment defines the tyranny's end.

terra: After recalling earlier generations destroyed by God, the ayah says criminals are not asked about their ذُنُوبِهِمْ; in context this marks judgment that needs no fact-finding, a boundary beside 21:23's broader accountability claim.

luna: The verse reserves the Hereafter's home for those who do not seek arrogance or corruption and says the end belongs to the God-fearing, a boundary to Thamud's destructive end. | terra: The final home is for those who seek neither self-exaltation nor corruption, and وَٱلْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ makes their good end the specific reverse of a corrupting people's ruin.
terra: A good deed receives better, while those who bring an evil are repaid only for what they did; the ayah states both the easy good end and the bounded bad sequel.
terra: Everything perishes except God, judgment belongs to Him, and all are returned to Him; nothing follows or outlasts the Owner's final ruling.

luna: The section names ذ ن ب as the root linking sin with an ill end; this verse says each community was seized for its own sin and lists distinct forms of ruin. | terra: فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنَا بِذَنبِهِ makes each destroyed people be seized by its own sin, then distinguishes the concrete forms in which that consequence arrived.
luna: The people ask for punishment to be hastened, but its term is appointed and it arrives suddenly, a warning-side parallel to Thamud's three-day notice.

luna: Punishment covers them from above and beneath their feet on the Day; this is a concrete counterpart to the section's encompassing punishment. | terra: Punishment covers them from above and from beneath their feet, and they are told to taste what they did; the surrounding penalty is explicitly their deed's result.
terra: People are told to inspect how the عَاقِبَة of stronger earlier civilizations followed their self-wronging despite messengers' proofs.

luna: Here the evil end of evildoers follows their denial and mockery of signs, a close parallel to the section's use of ukba for consequence. | terra: The عَاقِبَة of those who did evil is ٱلسُّوٓأَىٰ because they denied God's signs and mocked them; the ayah defines wrongdoing through the bad end carried by denial.
luna: The section says punishment comes because of the people's sin; this verse says corruption appears through what people's hands earned so they may taste some of what they did.
terra: Travel is commanded to see the عَاقِبَة of former peoples, most of whom associated partners with God; the lasting trace discloses the belief's consequence.
terra: People are commanded to set themselves toward the right religion before a day comes from God that cannot be repelled, making finality itself a preventive warning.
terra: One who submits to God while doing good grasps the firmest handhold, and to God belongs عَاقِبَةُ ٱلْأُمُورِ; sound action and the final end of affairs are joined.
luna: God gives a nearer punishment before the greater one so people may return, a warning-purpose parallel to the section's timed notice before Thamud's end.
terra: The disbelievers ask when the promise will arrive, reproducing the challenger's stance before the fixed answer in 34:30.
terra: The challengers are told they have an appointed day that they can delay or advance by no hour, sharpening the three-day promise's exact finality.
luna: What God opens of mercy cannot be withheld and what He withholds cannot be released after Him, extending the section's claim that His decision has no overrider.
terra: Whoever purifies himself does so only for his own good, and the destination is to God; purification is explicitly defined by whom its outcome returns to and where it ends.
terra: The reader is told to inspect the عَاقِبَة of stronger predecessors and is reminded that nothing can escape God, joining historical ends to irresistible power.

luna: The verse says God delays seizure for what people earn until an appointed term, then leaves no creature; it joins wrongdoing, respite, and consequence. | terra: If God took people for what they earned no creature would remain, but He defers them to an appointed term and then fully sees His servants; delay does not cancel consequence.
terra: Barriers are set before and behind the deniers and God covers them so they cannot see; this ayah tightly joins the section's bodily rearward image to the غ ش و covering branch.
terra: God records both what people sent ahead and their آثار, the tracks they leave behind; this offers a concrete trail-image for acts persisting into their later reckoning.
terra: If the Merciful intends harm, other gods' intercession cannot help and they cannot rescue, stating the no-reversal consequence against imagined rival owners.
terra: Each of the listed peoples denies the messengers and thereby makes God's punishment due, another direct formulation of warning rejected and consequence incurred.

luna: Canopies of fire lie above and beneath people; this gives a spatial form to the punishment that the section describes as covering them. | terra: Layers of fire lie above and below them, and بِذَٰلِكَ يُخَوِّفُ ٱللَّهُ عِبَادَهُ says God uses that enclosing end to warn His servants, joining covering punishment to divine fear-making.
terra: The idolaters are asked whether their gods could remove harm intended by God or withhold His mercy, testing both kinds of outcome against His sole authority.
terra: The evil results of what they earned become manifest and the punishment they mocked surrounds them, a direct formulation of the hidden end emerging from the act.
luna: This verse says the evil consequences of what people earned overtook them, a direct counterpart to the section's sin followed by its end.
luna: Every soul is paid in full for what it did, with God knowing what they do; this makes the section's consequence for sin a general rule of judgment.
terra: On the day all are exposed, God asks whose sovereignty is His and answers that it belongs to the One, the Subduer; 40:17 then makes this ownership the setting of final recompense.
terra: Every soul is repaid for what it earned, with no injustice and swift account, supplying the just consequence under the sole sovereignty declared in 40:16.

luna: The section says the Lord took Thamud for their sin; this verse likewise says God seized stronger earlier peoples for their sins, with no protector against Him. | terra: Earlier peoples were seized بِذُنُوبِهِمْ and had no protector against God; the causal phrase and failed defense both support the section's unavoidable aftermath.
terra: Messengers brought clear proofs, people disbelieved, and God seized them as strong and severe in punishment; this supplies the explanatory continuation of the sin-seizure in 40:21.
terra: An evil deed receives only its like, while righteous believers enter the Garden without measure; it sets the two opposed outcomes beside their generating acts.
luna: God saves the believing man from the plotters while severe punishment encompasses Pharaoh's people, joining the section's plot and enclosing-punishment images.
luna: The next verse shows Pharaoh's people exposed to the Fire morning and evening and then sent to the severest punishment, completing the consequence announced in 40:45.
terra: God's promise is true whether the Prophet is shown some threatened punishment or dies before it, since all return to God; non-observation does not undo the result.
terra: Earlier peoples were stronger and left more traces, yet their acquisitions did not avail; the instruction to inspect their عَاقِبَة makes achievement yield to final consequence.
luna: When people turn away, the Messenger is told to warn them of a thunderbolt like that which struck Aad and Thamud; this directly joins warning to the end of the named people.

luna: Thamud are guided but choose blindness, then are seized by a humiliating thunderbolt for what they earned, directly joining refusal, action, and consequence. | terra: Thamud choose blindness over guidance, so a thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seizes them بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ; choice and earned outcome are explicitly joined.
terra: Believers who were Godfearing are saved after Thamud is seized for what it earned in 41:17, separating the purified course from the guilty people's end.

luna: This verse states the moral boundary behind the section's outcome: good is for the doer, while evil is against the doer, and God wrongs no one. | terra: Whoever does good does it for himself and whoever does evil does it against himself, while the Lord is not unjust; the act already bears the direction of its end.

luna: The verse connects calamity to what hands have earned but adds that God pardons much, a boundary that keeps the section's punishment from implying every sin is immediately punished. | terra: Whatever affliction befalls people is because of what their hands earned, while God pardons much; it states the causal relation by which a painful aftermath follows the act.
terra: People are commanded to answer their Lord before a day comes from God that cannot be repelled, turning finality into the same preventive warning the section describes.
luna: After they deny messengers, God takes vengeance; the verse explicitly asks how the end of deniers was, echoing the section's question about outcomes.

luna: The passage announces visible smoke coming from the sky; 44:11 says it covers people and is painful punishment, completing this row's image. | terra: A manifest smoke is watched for in the sky, providing the visible substance that covers the people and is named painful punishment in 44:11.

luna: The smoke covers people and is called painful punishment, closely matching the section's covering language for a punishment that surrounds everyone. | terra: The manifest smoke of 44:10 يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ and is identified as a painful punishment, giving the covering-punishment relation a visible collective form.

luna: Every soul is recompensed for what it earned without being wronged, a direct formulation of the section's deed-and-consequence relation. | terra: God creates heaven and earth in truth so that every soul may be repaid for what it earned without injustice, joining the Owner-Creator directly to just consequence.
terra: One who takes desire as god is knowingly left astray with a covering over sight; the visual cover is a present consequence of chosen misrule under God's judgment.
terra: The evil results of their deeds appear and what they mocked encloses them, repeating the section's movement from crime to an all-around sequel.
terra: God's sovereignty over heaven and earth is again followed immediately by forgiveness or punishment according to His will, reinforcing ownership as the setting of recompense.
terra: Thamud and the other named peoples deny their messengers, so God's threat becomes due; denial is followed by a promised consequence in compressed form.
luna: The section reads ukba as a final consequence no one can reverse; here God says His word cannot be changed and He is not unjust to servants.
luna: The section says God's threat is meant to make people cautious; this verse tells the Messenger to remind by the Quran whoever fears God's warning.
terra: What the addressees are promised is declared true, supporting the section's insistence that the post-crime promise cannot be falsified.
terra: Judgment is declared certain to occur immediately after the promise is called true in 51:5, identifying the promise's unavoidable content.
terra: Thamud are told to enjoy themselves only until a stated time, another formulation of the limited interval between the offense and its promised end.
terra: They rebel against their Lord's command, and the thunderbolt takes them while they look on; the verse makes defiance and consequence one continuous scene.
terra: They can neither rise nor obtain help after the thunderbolt, showing that nothing can turn back the judgment once its end arrives.

terra: ذَنُوبًا here means an allotted share rather than sins: wrongdoers have a share like their predecessors', so the source section's root sounds within a promised portion of the very consequence it describes.
terra: The punishment of the Lord is declared certain to occur, the promised finality whose second half is supplied by 52:8.
terra: مَا لَهُۥ مِن دَافِعٍ says the certain punishment of 52:7 has no repeller, matching the section's claim that no one can turn back the end.

luna: This verse states both sides of the section's moral outcome: wrongdoers are repaid for what they did and those who do good receive the best. | terra: Heaven and earth belong to God so that He may recompense evildoers for what they did and reward good-doers with the best, explicitly deriving the two outcomes from His ownership.
terra: A person has only what he strove for, grounding the consequence completed in 53:40-41 in the person's own act.
terra: Human striving will be seen, making the once-hidden deed visible before its full repayment in 53:41.
terra: The striving shown in 53:40 is repaid with the fullest recompense, completing the sequence from act to terminal return.
terra: God destroys Thamud and leaves none, restating the total reach of the Lord's recompense after the camel crime.

luna: The root غ ش و named in the section reappears as the overturned towns are covered by what covers them, a direct image of ruin enveloping its victims. | terra: After the overturned cities are cast down in 53:53, فَغَشَّىٰهَا مَا غَشَّىٰ makes an unnamed covering complete their destruction, another punitive use of the section's covering root.
luna: Thamud deny the warnings; this is the rejection that precedes the she-camel test and slaughter in the same passage.
luna: Thamud reject following one human like themselves, a specific form of denial before the camel test and slaughter in this passage.
luna: They question why revelation came to Salih and call him a liar, completing the rejection that 54:23 names before the camel appears.
luna: After the denial in 54:23, the verse says they will learn who is the arrogant liar, anticipating the camel episode and its outcome.

luna: God sends the she-camel as a trial and says to await what happens, paralleling the section's sign as a warning before the reckoning. | terra: God says He is sending the camel as a trial and commands watchful patience, making the animal itself the warning-sign before Thamud's choice.

luna: The water is divided between the people and the camel, clarifying the provision they violate when they later hamstring her. | terra: The water is apportioned and every share must be attended, specifying the owner's measured provision that the attack on the camel disrupts in 54:29.

luna: They call their companion, who takes the task and hamstrings the camel; this is the offense before the announced punishment. | terra: They call their companion, who takes hold and hamstrings the camel; this is the offense whose warned consequence the next two ayat unfold.

luna: After the camel is hamstrung, this refrain asks how God's punishment and warnings turned out, framing the next verse's cry as fulfillment. | terra: God asks how His punishment and warnings were, explicitly interpreting the camel event in 54:27-29 as warning followed by punishment.

luna: A single cry leaves them like dry brush, a specific account of the enveloping punishment that follows their act. | terra: A single blast reduces the people to dry crushed material after the hamstringing, a vivid form of the total leveling named in 91:14.
luna: All dominion belongs to God and all affairs return to Him; this links the Lord's ownership in the section with its focus on where an affair ends.
luna: The section's account of Thamud's consequence meets this verse's phrase ذاقوا وبال أمرهم: earlier deniers tasted the evil consequence of their affair and face painful punishment.

luna: The verse commands believers to fear God and consider what each soul has sent ahead for tomorrow, making the future consequence of present acts explicit. | terra: Every soul is commanded to inspect what it has sent ahead for tomorrow, recasting the section's consequence-behind-the-act as a deed already dispatched toward its doer.
luna: This verse uses the same formulation وبال أمرهم for the evil consequence of disbelief, closely matching the section's link between sin and what follows it.
luna: The preceding verse says a town rebelled against its Lord's command, was strictly called to account, and was punished, completing 65:9's evil consequence.
luna: The section names ع ق ب as end and recompense; this verse says the disobedient town tasted the evil consequence of its affair and that its عاقبة was loss.
luna: After the account and loss in 65:8-9, this verse addresses people of understanding with a command to fear God and announces a reminder sent down to them.
luna: The section's Lord as owner of the camel meets this verse's declaration that dominion is in God's hand and He has power over all things.
terra: The inhabitants of the Blaze confess their ذَنب, and exclusion is pronounced on them; confession and the sin's terminal punishment stand in the same ayah.
terra: Those on earth are asked whether they feel secure from being made to sink into the shaking ground, another warning against the offender's misplaced lack of fear.
terra: They are asked whether they feel secure from a stone-bearing storm and are told they will know how God's warning is, joining threatened sign and fear-making.
terra: Earlier peoples denied, and the ayah asks how God's rejection of them was; it supplies the historical consequence behind the warning in 67:16-17.
luna: This verse names Thamud among the peoples who denied the overwhelming event, connecting their denial to the destruction described next.

luna: Thamud are destroyed by the overpowering blast, another specific account of their end after rejecting warning. | terra: Thamud are destroyed by the overwhelming blast, a compressed statement of the people's terminal consequence.
terra: A questioner asks for the punishment that is bound to fall, staging a demanded consequence like Thamud's challenge before 70:2 states its unavoidability.
terra: The punishment for the disbelievers has no averter, directly matching the irrevocable outcome attached to denial.
luna: The verse explicitly attributes drowning and entry into the Fire to their sins, compressing the section's sequence of offense followed by punishment.
terra: Those who believe in their Lord fear neither loss nor oppressive burden, a good-outcome counterpart to the offender who rightly expects a harmful sequel.

luna: Every soul is held for what it earned, an explicit image of personal accountability that fits the section's sin and its following consequence. | terra: Every soul is held in pledge for what it earned, giving bodily force to the section's claim that the deed remains attached until its consequence.
terra: A person will be told what he sent ahead and left behind, placing the complete account on both temporal sides of the body-like image developed in the section.
terra: What people are promised is certain to occur, a compact parallel to the unfalsifiable word given after the camel's killing.
luna: Moses is sent to Pharaoh because he has transgressed, introducing the warning-and-purification exchange that the section's 79:18 parallel continues.

luna: Moses asks Pharaoh whether he will purify himself, putting the section's ز ك و theme beside a ruler who rejects warning and meets punishment. | terra: Moses offers Pharaoh the possibility that he might purify himself; 79:21-25 then show denial taking him to the opposite end, so purification and outcome meet within one scene.
luna: Moses offers to guide Pharaoh to his Lord so that he may fear Him, completing the warning purpose before the sign in 79:20.
luna: Moses shows Pharaoh the great sign, the specific warning sign before the denial and disobedience in 79:21.

luna: Pharaoh denies and disobeys after seeing the sign, the offense that precedes his exemplary seizure. | terra: Pharaoh denies and disobeys after the offer of purification in 79:18, specifying the guilty turn whose result arrives in 79:25.
luna: Pharaoh then turns away and strives against the warning, continuing the rejection whose outcome appears in 79:25.
luna: Pharaoh gathers his people and calls out before claiming lordship in 79:24, completing the immediate scene before his punishment.

luna: Pharaoh's claim to be the highest lord follows the purification invitation in 79:18 and defines his rebellion before the exemplary seizure in 79:25. | terra: Pharaoh proclaims himself the highest lord, making false ownership and lordship the offense immediately before the true God seizes him.

luna: God seizes Pharaoh with exemplary punishment, a clear offense-to-end sequence. | terra: God seizes Pharaoh with the exemplary punishment of the latter and the former after his refusal to purify and claim to lordship, directly staging deed followed by recompense.
luna: The preceding punishment is called a lesson for whoever fears, matching the section's point that warning is meant to make its hearer cautious.
luna: Where 91:15 says the Lord does not fear His consequence, this verse places fear of standing before the Lord in the human being, who then restrains the soul from desire.
luna: This completes the preceding verse's human fear and restraint with its outcome: the Garden is the refuge, a positive end after self-discipline.
terra: The murdered girl is asked for what ذَنبٍ she was killed; the unanswered question marks the boundary that a just punishment follows an actual offense, not an innocent victim.
terra: Each soul will know what it sent ahead and left behind, a parallel formulation of deeds retaining a rearward remainder that appears at the final accounting.
terra: No soul owns anything for another on the Day, and the command belongs wholly to God, isolating the Owner whose judgment no one can answer or reverse.
terra: What people were earning forms a rust-like covering over their hearts, so their own repeated acts become the cover that precedes the fire of 83:16.
terra: They enter Hell after their earnings have coated their hearts in 83:14, turning that inward covering into its final punitive result.
terra: The condemned person receives his record from behind his back, giving literal bodily placement to the deed-account whose painful end follows in 84:11-12.
terra: The recipient of the record behind his back calls for destruction, contributing the immediate recognition of the bad end attached to that rearward record.
terra: He enters a blazing fire after receiving the record behind his back, completing the bodily sequence from recorded deeds to their consequence.
terra: Thamud are named with Pharaoh immediately before 85:19-20 describe deniers whom God encompasses from behind; this ayah supplies the specific people for that rearward scene.
terra: The named peoples' ongoing denial is stated just before God encompasses them from behind in 85:20, contributing the offense to which that enclosing position answers.
terra: وَٱللَّهُ مِن وَرَآئِهِم مُّحِيطٌ places God behind the persistent deniers and encompassing them, a striking nonlexical meeting of the section's rear/heel and all-covering judgment images.
luna: This verse says the one who fears will take the reminder, matching the section's account of divine warning as an invitation to caution.
luna: Where 87:10 says the one who fears will heed the reminder, this verse says the most wretched avoids it, a direct boundary between response and rejection.
luna: The one who avoids the reminder enters the great Fire, making the negative outcome of refusing warning explicit.
luna: The following verse says the entrant neither dies nor lives there, specifying the Fire's lasting consequence after 87:12.

luna: The close wording قد أفلح من تزكى repeats the section's claim that the one who purifies the soul succeeds, giving its positive side a parallel formulation. | terra: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ repeats both purification and success from 91:9, and 87:16-17 immediately disclose why that purified course has the better end.
luna: After the purification and success stated in 87:14, this verse adds remembrance of the Lord and prayer as the continuing shape of that successful course.

luna: The passage says people prefer the nearer life, a specific choice that can leave the lasting outcome the section calls ukba out of view. | terra: People prefer the nearer worldly life immediately after 87:14 praises purification, identifying the short preference that can obscure the purified person's true outcome.

luna: The Hereafter is better and more lasting than the nearer life, giving the section's end-focused image an explicit lasting horizon. | terra: The Hereafter is better and more lasting than the nearer life of 87:16, clarifying why purification in 87:14 has the end that remains rather than the one that passes.

luna: The section describes غاشية as a covering punishment; this surah opens by naming the overwhelming event الغاشية, whose next verses describe its faces and fire. | terra: ٱلْغَاشِيَةِ names the overwhelming event whose following verses describe humbled faces and fire, extending the section's غ ش و branch from night's cover to eschatological punishment.
luna: This verse begins the description of those met by الغاشية: faces are humbled, giving a human consequence to the event named in 88:1.
luna: The same passage specifies the fire entered by the humbled faces, making explicit one punishment encompassed by الغاشية.
luna: The passage adds a boiling spring for those humbled by الغاشية, another concrete feature of the punishment named in 88:1.
luna: After recalling Aad and Thamud, the verse says God poured on them a scourge of punishment, a concise parallel to the Lord's retribution for Thamud's offense.
luna: The verse says the Fire is closed over the people of the left, an enclosing punishment that bounds the section's covering image.
terra: وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ repeats the section's night-covering act almost verbatim, and this surah then divides human striving by the ease or hardship to which it leads.
luna: This verse pairs giving with fear of God, the beginning of a good path and outcome that answers the section's contrast between purification and sin.
luna: The giver's belief in the best completes the positive course begun in 92:5, helping specify the belief behind the ease that follows in 92:7.

luna: The one who gives and believes in the best is made easy toward ease, completing the positive consequence introduced in 92:5. | terra: God promises to ease the giving, Godfearing believer of 92:5-6 toward ease, directly expressing the section's good, non-heavy end of purification.
luna: This begins the opposite course: withholding and thinking oneself self-sufficient, a boundary against the section's successful purification.
luna: The withholding person also denies the best; the verse makes the moral reversal explicit before the hard outcome in 92:10.

luna: The withheld-and-denying course is made easy toward hardship, a direct negative counterpart to the eased course of 92:7. | terra: God eases the miserly denier of 92:8-9 toward hardship, giving the negative counterpart: a chosen act carries a hard end behind it.
luna: When the miser falls, his wealth does not avail him; this makes the bad course's end concrete rather than merely naming it.
luna: The passage says guidance belongs to God before describing the two courses and their ends, locating the section's warning within divine guidance.
luna: The verse says the first life and the Hereafter belong to God, connecting the section's Lord-as-owner with the final outcomes that follow deeds.
luna: The passage warns of a blazing Fire after describing the two paths, giving the consequence side of the section's sin-and-outcome image.
luna: The Fire is for the most wretched, a concrete negative end set against the ease and purification in the surrounding passage.
luna: The one entering that end is the person who denied and turned away, directly matching the section's denial-before-punishment sequence.
luna: The most God-conscious person is kept away from the Fire, the positive boundary opposite the punished denier.
luna: The verse describes giving wealth in order to purify oneself; the source section's root ز ك و names purification as the way to success.
luna: This verse says the giver is not repaying a favor, clarifying the pure motive in the positive course that contrasts with the section's consequence for sin.
luna: The giver seeks the face of the Most High Lord, specifying the orientation of the purification that the preceding verses contrast with denial.
luna: The passage ends by promising that the giver will be satisfied, giving the positive course its own outcome beside the section's punishment image.

luna: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, a precise statement that deeds leave an outcome, paired with the next verse's evil deed. | terra: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, making even the smallest sound act persist to its favorable outcome.

luna: Whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it, making the section's sin followed by its consequence explicit at the smallest scale. | terra: Whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it, a minimal and exact statement that an offense remains until it meets its doer.

luna: This verse says the Fire is closed over the hoarder named in the preceding passage; 104:9 describes its extended columns completing the enclosure. | terra: The kindled fire is closed over the offenders, another concrete form of punishment enclosing those whose preceding acts brought it.
luna: The preceding verse closes the Fire over the hoarder, and this one describes its columns extended over them, making the enclosing punishment concrete.
